To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the RD29X promoter elements were activated in soybean under drought stress conditions.

(1) both Arabidopsis RD promoter elements were active in soybean; (2) RD29A promoter showed constitutive activity under normal conditions; and (3) RD29A and B promoter activity were significantly induced in response to water stress in soybean.
the RD29A and B promoters from Arabidopsis are activated in soybean under dry-down conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of drought-responsive promoters from model plants that may be suitable for the development of drought-tolerant soybean cultivars.
the identification and characterization of promoter elements in soybeans that are responsive to abiotic stress.
the identification of stress-inducible promoters in soybean that could be used in transgenic strategies to improve abiotic stress tolerance in this crop.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
both the RD29A and B promoters are active in soybean, and that their activity increases in response to water stress.

both RD29X promoters are active under drought stress and can be used for the engineering of drought tolerance into soybean plants, but the level of constitutive expression of the RD29A promoter may be a concern for the expression of transgenes under control of this element.
both RD29A and B promoters can be used to drive transgenes in soybean to mitigate abiotic stresses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
both promoters are responsive to water stress in soybean and that the RD29A promoter is more responsive to drought stress than the RD29B promoter.
RD29A and B promoters are activated in soybean under dry-down conditions and that these promoters may be useful to drive expression of transgenes in soybean to improve abiotic stress tolerance.
both RD29A and B promoters are activated in soybean, albeit with a low constitutive activity, and that the activity of these promoters in roots is greater than in leaves.

both promoters can be used for the generation of transgenic soybean plants with enhanced drought tolerance.
